title: Gatekeeper: Launch Authorization & Exception Encoder
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a compact, machine-friendly decision and logging pattern we call the Gatekeeper Encoder. It standardizes: (a) release authorization checkpoints, (b) exception approval metadata, (c) RBAC v2 verification steps, (d) audit-log field set and SIEM export mapping, and (e) evidence automation hooks needed for compliance-ready launches.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: applies to any production-facing release (hosted API, Dedicated, Private) that touches customer data, RBAC, networking, or persistence.
- Intent: reduce ad-hoc exception emails by encoding approvals and evidence into a small, queryable payload emitted at release gate transitions and into the audit pipeline.
- This is a hybrid doc: prescriptive checklist + example payload schema + approval workflow.

Quick decision flow (high level):
1) Owner fills pre-launch encoder payload and attaches artifact list (build id, infra diff, eval run id).
2) Security reviews RBAC v2 delta, SIEM/retention impact, and evidence readiness.
3) If approval needed, Gatekeeper creates an exception ticketable payload with TTL and compensating controls.
4) Signoff occurs (automated recording to audit stream) and release proceeds.

Pre-launch checklist (owner responsibilities) — minimal pass to request approval:
- Release manifest (build id + commit): present (owner)
- Threat surface summary: brief bullet list of new endpoints/scopes (owner)
- RBAC v2 delta: list of roles changed, new role bindings, any wildcard grants (owner)
- Audit-log hooks validated: every new API path emits request_id, actor_id, role_snapshot, action, resource_id, timestamp (owner/eng)
- SIEM mapping stub: fields mapped to SIEM ingest (owner/sec-eng)
- Evidence snapshot: config/terraform plan, container image digest, eval report (quality+regressions), automated artifact hashes (owner)
- Rollback plan: explicit trigger metrics + owner contact (owner/sre)

RBAC v2 verification matrix (example checks and expected outputs):
- Check: New role definitions include allow/deny and expiry? -> Expected: deny-by-default, no persistent wildcards
- Check: Role binding scope (org / team / service) documented? -> Expected: explicit principal list with justification ticket
- Check: Service principals limited to least privilege? -> Expected: yes or documented exception with TTL and compensating control
- Machine-check: run rbac-diff tool (ticket SEC-742) and attach diff summary (SHA).
- Manual checks: Security to verify any policy that changes management-plane access.

Audit log payload (recommended canonical fields):
- event_id: opaque UUID
- timestamp_utc: iso8601
- actor_id: user|service principal id
- actor_role_snapshot: list of role ids at time of event (RBACv2 snapshot)
- action_type: string (e.g., release.request, release.signoff, exception.create)
- resource: release:build:<build-id> | model:<model-id> | infra:stack:<stack-id>
- decision: approve | deny | exception-granted
- decision_by: principal id(s) who approved
- decision_ttl: iso8601 or duration (for exceptions)
- evidence_refs: list of artifact ids (s3 path, object id)
- justification: free text (short)
- trace_id: correlated request trace id (if available)

Notes on audit schema design: keep fields shallow and flat so SIEM can index and alert easily. actor_role_snapshot should be a short array of role ids, not full policy documents. Record role snapshots to enable repro of who had privileges at approval time.

SIEM export mapping and retention guidance:
- Map event_id -> siem.event_id, timestamp_utc -> @timestamp, actor_id -> user.id, action_type -> event.action, decision -> event.outcome, evidence_refs -> file.references
- Ensure retention tags are attached by environment (prod=7y-hardened, sandbox=90d). For exports to 3rd-party SIEM, include a signed manifest hash to verify non-tampering.
- Redact sensitive fields before export (PII in justification) but keep hashes/pointers to original evidence in internal long-term store.

Evidence automation runbook (baseline):
- Trigger point: when release manifest status moves to "signoff_requested"; CI pipeline emits encoder payload to "release-gate" topic.
- Automated steps:
  - Snapshot: capture terraform plan output, k8s manifests, image digest -> store in evidence-bucket/release/<build-id>/
  - Hashing: compute sha256 for each artifact and include in evidence_refs with metadata: {path, sha256, size}
  - Eval results: attach eval-run id and summary CSV (metric deltas)
  - Chain-of-custody: signer (security approver) mints a signed approval token stored in evidence-bucket and referenced by audit payload
- Storage: evidence-bucket encrypts with customer/KMS keys where required; small TTL for sandbox, long for prod (see SIEM guidance).

Exception approval flow (minimal encoded policy):
- Criteria to grant exception:
  - Business criticality documented and timeboxed
  - Compensating control in place (e.g., increased monitoring, IP allowlist, MFA enforcement)
  - Expiry/renewal schedule defined
- Approvers: at least one security engineer and one product/owner or SRE for infra exceptions
- Encoding: exception payload must include: exception_id, reason, owner, compensating_controls (short list), expiry_timestamp, mitigation_actions, related_jira
- TTL policy: default 72 hours for low-risk grants, up to 30 days for higher-risk with escalation path to security leadership

Sign-off template (pasteable):
- release_id: <build-id>
- owner: <name>
- sro_contact: <name/email>
- security_reviewer: <name> (link to ticket)
- signoff_decision: APPROVE | DENY | EXCEPTION
- signoff_justification: <short summary>
- evidence_refs: [s3://evidence/release/<build-id>/*]
- signature_hash: sha256(signer_id + release_id + timestamp)

Post-launch window and observability hooks:
- Monitoring window: 72 hours by default. Define critical KPIs (error_rate, latency_p50/p95, auth_failures, anomalous_access).
- Auto-signal rollback: if auth_failures spike > 10x baseline or error_rate > X% for N minutes, auto-open rollback playbook and ping oncall.
- Audit stream: ensure release.signoff events are routed to high-fidelity index for 30-day rapid search and long-term archive for compliance retention.

Appendix: example encoder payload (pseudo-JSON compact representation)
- note: below is an example to show shape only; actual audit record must be emitted as flattened fields to the audit pipeline.

{
  "event_id": "uuid-1234",
  "timestamp_utc": "2026-03-01T15:23:00Z",
  "actor_id": "maya.chen",
  "actor_role_snapshot": ["sec-admin","eng-release"],
  "action_type": "release.signoff",
  "resource": "release:build:2026-03-01-9812",
  "decision": "approve",
  "decision_by": ["maya.chen","liam.oconnor"],
  "evidence_refs": ["s3://evidence/release/2026-03-01-9812/terraform-plan.json#sha256:abcd..."],
  "justification": "Validated RBAC delta and eval metrics; low risk; monitoring window 72h",
  "trace_id": "trace-xyz"
}

Open questions / TODOs: (for review)
- Should exception payload include a risk score (0-100) emitted to SIEM for alert thresholds? (ops/security decision)
- Standardize TTLs per exception type (infra vs data-plane vs model-access) - propose table by next EOW
- Decide canonical storage for evidence snapshots (S3 vs internal artifact store) and who can request deletions

Next steps:
- Security to review and sign off on audit field list (assign: Priya)
- Infra to adapt rbac-diff output into evidence_refs (assign: Diego)
- SRE to wire alert rules to event.action=="release.signoff" and anomalous auth metrics (assign: Samantha)
- Owner to prototype encoder emission in CI for one upcoming non-critical release (owner: Maya)

Related tickets and references:
- SEC-742 (rbac-diff automation)
- SEC-781 (siem retention mapping proposal)
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1832

Notes-to-self (working):
- Keep payload minimal and audit-index-friendly. We can expand fields later, but for now avoid embedding policy documents inline.
- This doc should become the source for a small encoder library in /infra/tools/release-gate that emits the canonical audit record.

End of working draft.
